title: Hivemind in Code: Do Open Models Generate the Same Bug?

original_idea.body:
# Hivemind in Code: Do Open Models Generate the Same Bug?

**Problem:** LLM coding assistants sharing reasoning patterns may independently introduce homologous bugs. The Hivemind output-similarity method has not been applied to code.

**Direction:** Give 6-8 open code models security-sensitive coding prompts and measure how often multiple models produce the same insecure pattern and inter-model code similarity via AST/token overlap. Twist: focus on whether insecure completions are more homogeneous than secure ones.

**Why it matters:** Correlated insecure code suggestions mean a single bad pattern propagates across all teams using LLM assistants.

**Relevant context:** Applies Artificial Hivemind to code; open code models (Qwen2.5-Coder, CodeLlama) and free static analysis.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible supply-chain risk (shared insecure patterns) but indirect catastrophic-AI link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Code generation plus off-the-shelf static analysis and AST/token overlap; accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: are insecure completions more homogeneous; clear metric and prompts.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open code models and free analyzers; correlated-insecurity angle labs underweight.

novelty.reasoning: Homogeneity lens applied to code is a fresh-ish slice; related observations exist.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Code-variance noted; cross-model shared-insecure-pattern measurement partly open.
